doc.title: Steve Buckingham, interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 25, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Preparing songs with artists, overcutting and hidden gems
summary: He prepares with demos, picks songs with the artist, overcuts for vinyl length, and notes culled tracks show up as hidden gems.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: What’s the first run through of the songs like? Do you have a piano player on hand or did you play your guitar?
Well you mean when I met with like her with the songs?

I had demos. I had demo tapes. Now Melissa is a great piano player but usually when I’d meet with an artist I’d have demo tapes of songs. A lot of times, like with Dolly or somebody, they’re great writers. Melissa is a good writer, a great writer. And they would always have input about their songs. And it would be again like yes, no, I hear this I don’t hear that one. And it’s just a process you go through. And it would be very methodical and very thorough so that when you got to the studio there was not going to be any surprises. You had your material picked. Well you’d always overcut as we said. Because on vinyl you had 17 minutes a side. You could do five or six cuts per side on a vinyl album. After that it just wouldn’t hold it on the inside grooves. But you would cut 15 or 16 songs to pick your 10 or 12 on every project I ever did I think. I think, for sure. You cull them out as they say for the end.
Did the things that got culled out ever make it to the next record.
Not that I know of. I know they’ve done like re-releases on things, later re-releases. Hidden gems.
Hidden gems. Now we have more time on the CD we can pull in —

Yeah. And they do that sort of thing. And occasionally I will hear something that we recorded and mixed but it didn’t make the album but it turns up on somebody’s hidden gems album or whatever you want to call those things. Unreleased.
